summary: Ran `npx -y -p @angular/cli@15 ng update @angular/core@15 @angular/cli@15 --allow-dirty --force` from EFNgApp/EFNgApp/ClientApp on Node 18/npm 10 (the hop's required Node version was already active). This bumped the @angular/* packages to 15.2.10, the CLI/build-angular toolchain to 15.2.11, and TypeScript to ~4.9.5, and applied Angular's own migrations: removed the deprecated `relativeLinkResolution: 'legacy'` router option, dropped the now-CLI-owned `renderModule` re-export from main.server.ts (keeping `renderModuleFactory`), removed the obsolete `require.context` test-discovery boilerplate from test.ts (Angular 15's Karma builder finds specs itself), and set tsconfig `target`/`useDefineForClassFields` to the new ES2022/false IDE defaults. The hop file listed no related packages needing a bump. Install and build both pass; test fails the exact same pre-existing way as baseline and every prior hop (angular.json's test target points at a nonexistent root-level styles.css instead of src/styles.css), so no new regression was introduced.
changes: Angular core migration: removed the deprecated `relativeLinkResolution: 'legacy'` RouterModule.forRoot option in src/app/app.module.ts
Angular CLI migration: removed the `renderModule` re-export from src/main.server.ts (now owned by the Angular CLI itself), keeping `renderModuleFactory`
Angular CLI migration: removed the obsolete `require.context`-based spec loading boilerplate from src/test.ts
Angular CLI migration: removed the now-redundant `target: es2016` override from src/tsconfig.server.json
Angular CLI migration: set tsconfig.json compiler `target` to ES2022 and added `useDefineForClassFields: false` (IDE-only settings; actual output ECMA version is still controlled by Browserslist)
package-lock.json regenerated by npm as part of the update/install cycle
manual_followups: npm install still needs legacy-peer-deps (set project-wide via ClientApp/.npmrc in an earlier hop) because @ngrx/*@^8.5.2 and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0 declare peers on @angular/core ^8/^7; this hop again found no required bump for them. They should move to Angular-15-compatible majors in a later hop, at which point the .npmrc override can likely be removed.

`npm run test` fails before any spec executes because angular.json's test architect target still points at `styles.css` at the ClientApp root instead of `src/styles.css`; this predates this hop (present since baseline) and was left as-is per the rule that pre-existing failures don't need fixing.

@ngrx/store, @ngrx/effects, and @ngrx/store-devtools are still pre-Ivy ('View Engine') libraries per the build log; they continue to build under Angular 15's backwards-compatibility support but should be upgraded (alongside the peer-dependency fix above) before Ivy-only tooling drops this support.
